info.title: SunApps MES
info.description: Plant-floor MES service for the IdaMilk creamery. Cron jobs poll the AVEVA Historian for separator batches, bulk milk intake, blend tanks, surge tanks and equipment state, turn them into NetSuite work orders / issues / completions / inventory adjustments, and record every batch locally. On top of that it exposes a rich read-only /api/historian query gateway over the plant historian, live status and analytics feeds for the SunApps UI, operator review endpoints for batches that failed to post to NetSuite, a BOM admin surface, and a replay (time-travel simulation) control panel.

post.description: Posts an assembly unbuild to NetSuite for a milk separation — raw milk consumed, skim and cream produced. This is the low-level NetSuite write that `/api/mes/milk/separation/batch` calls into after it has recorded the batch locally; exposed directly for manual correction. Writes to live NetSuite.

schema.description: Items, quantities and lots for the unbuild.

schema.description: Item, quantity, location and bin for the work order.

post.description: Records a completed cold-milk separator batch and posts it to NetSuite as an assembly unbuild (raw milk in → skim + cream out). Called by the separation cron job once the separator state machine sees a run finish. If the NetSuite post fails, or a product index cannot be mapped to an item, the batch is stored with status `pending_ns` / `error` and surfaces in the Separation Review queue.

schema.description: Raw batch payload — work order, lots, product indices, and skim/cream quantities read off the historian.

200.description: Batch processed (check `success` in the body — a held batch also returns 200).

post.summary: Ingest a bulk milk flow reading
post.description: Records a bulk milk intake totalizer reading from an unload bay and consumes the corresponding quantity against the registered bulk milk work order. Called by the bulk milk cron job.

schema.description: Bay number, destination silo, product code, and totalized unload quantity.

get.description: Recorded separator batches, newest first. The Separation Review screen filters on `status` to pull just the backlog.

The separator HMI's product config (indices 1-40) mapped to NetSuite items. Populates the edit dropdowns on the Separation Review screen so an operator can correct a mis-read product index before retrying a batch.

post.description: Re-posts a `pending_ns` / `error` separation batch to NetSuite, optionally with operator-corrected product indices. Writes to live NetSuite.

200.description: Retry attempted — response carries the NetSuite result and the updated batch.

post.description: Dismisses a `pending_ns` / `error` batch so it stops appearing in the review queue. Nothing is posted to NetSuite.
Binds a NetSuite bulk milk work order to an unload bay so subsequent flow readings auto-consume against it. Called from the SunApps UI when an operator starts an unload.

schema.description: Work order, bay, silo, and item details for the run.

post.description: Closes out a registered bulk milk run and finishes its NetSuite work order.

schema.description: Identifies the run to complete, plus final quantities.

get.description: Registered runs that are still accepting flow readings.

post.summary: Ingest a blend tank WO start
post.description: Opens a blend tank batch when the tank's HMI signals a work order start. Called by the blend tank cron job. Resolves the product name off the tank to a NetSuite item; an unresolvable product holds the batch for review.

schema.description: Tank id, work order, product name, and start timestamp.

500.description: Failed to process the WO start.

post.summary: Ingest a blend tank WO end
post.description: Closes a blend tank batch and posts its completion to NetSuite. Called by the blend tank cron job when the tank's HMI signals the work order finished.

schema.description: Tank id, work order, final quantity, and end timestamp.

500.description: Failed to process the WO end.

post.description: Records an inflow totalizer reading for one of the lines feeding a blend tank, so the batch accumulates which ingredients (and how much of each) went in. Drives the automatic ingredient issues against the work order.

schema.description: Tank id, line id, source silo/product, and totalized flow.

post.description: Closes blend tank batches still marked active but with no NetSuite work order behind them — leftovers from a crash or a mis-fired start event. Administrative cleanup; takes no body.

get.description: Everything the pollers currently believe about the plant floor. Served from the in-memory status store (hydrated from the DB at boot), so it is cheap enough for the dashboard to poll on a short interval. Sections are null until their first poll completes (HTTP serves before hydration finishes) and each carries its own pollAt. Reflects the sim clock while replay mode is on.

schema.description: Snapshot keyed by subsystem — separator, blendTanks (tanks + lines), bulkMilk, silos (levels merged with derived activity), uhts, surgeTanks, fillers (Filler 1 inlet meter — inletGpm, inletTotalizerGal, measured, running, sampleAt), recentBatches, recentBlendBatches, recentSurgeBatches, tick, lastPoll, eventCount.

get.description: The in-memory rolling log of notable poller events (batch starts and ends, state transitions, NetSuite posts, errors). Non-durable — it is empty after a restart and is cleared by the replay reset.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only return events after this timestamp (ISO 8601).

get.description: Substring search over the Historian `Tags` entity — returns every tag whose fully-qualified name contains `q`. Follows OData `@odata.nextLink` pages until `limit` is reached. The install carries ~23,000 tags, so always pass a narrowing `q`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Substring to match against the tag FQN, e.g. `MSILO` or `Separator.`.

get.description: Reads the tag's latest archived value from the Historian `ProcessValues` entity.

404.description: No value available for that tag.

get.description: Reads the current value of each requested tag in parallel. Every result is also written into the in-memory poll store, so repeated calls build up a queryable series retrievable via `/api/historian/polled-history/{fqn}` — useful for tags the Historian archives too infrequently to trend.

200.description: One entry per requested tag (`value` is null when unavailable).

get.description: Trend data for one tag over a time window. For non-raw resolutions the route first tries `AnalogSummary` (native Historian aggregation); if that errors or returns no rows it falls back to raw `ProcessValues` and step-resamples them server-side, carrying each last-known value forward and marking the synthesised points `interpolated: true`. The `source` field in the response says which path was taken. Aggregation requires `since` — without it the request is always served raw. Results are capped at 100,000 rows.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Window start (ISO 8601). Required for any non-raw resolution.

200.description: The series, plus a `_debug` block listing each OData page fetched.

items.description: AnalogSummary rows carry Average/Minimum/Maximum/Count and `_summary: true`; resampled ProcessValues rows carry `interpolated: true`.

get.description: Runs the same separator-batch extraction the separation cron job uses, straight against the historian. Read-only — unlike the cron job this does not persist anything or post to NetSuite, so it is safe for ad-hoc inspection.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Window start (ISO 8601). Defaults to 24 hours ago.

get.description: Returns values for a tag from the in-memory poll store rather than the Historian archive. The store is filled by calls to `/api/historian/tags`, which supplements tags the Historian archives too infrequently to trend usefully. The store is process-local and non-durable — it is empty after a restart and is cleared by the replay reset.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Window start (ISO 8601). Omit for everything held.

200.description: Polled values (empty if the tag was never polled).

get.description: Lists every tag currently held in the in-memory poll store and how many points each has.

Everything the Historian knows about a tag — the `Tags` row (TagType, EngUnit, min/max, interpolation type, source) plus its extended properties. The extended properties lookup is best-effort: `TagExtendedProperties` 404s on some Historian installs, in which case `extendedProps` comes back empty rather than failing.

get.summary: Statistical summary for an analog tag
get.description: Raw `AnalogSummary` rows for an analog tag — First/Last, Minimum/Maximum with their timestamps, Average, StdDev, Integral, Count and PercentGood per interval. Unlike `/history/{fqn}` this returns the Historian's rows untouched, with no normalisation or ProcessValues fallback. Results are capped at 100,000 rows.

parameters.name: fqn
parameters.description: Fully-qualified tag name of an analog tag.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Window start (ISO 8601). Defaults to 24 hours ago.

parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: Interval size in MILLISECONDS (not a keyword). Default 3600000 = 1 hour.

get.summary: Time-in-state summary for a discrete tag
get.description: Raw `StateSummary` rows — how long a discrete or string tag spent in each state per interval. This is the primitive behind the filler-hours report. Results are capped at 100,000 rows.

parameters.name: fqn
parameters.description: Fully-qualified tag name of a discrete or string tag.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Window start (ISO 8601). Defaults to 24 hours ago.

parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: Interval size in MILLISECONDS. Default 3600000 = 1 hour.

get.description: Queries the Historian `Events` entity, newest first, with optional type and source filters.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Window start (ISO 8601, exclusive). Defaults to 24 hours ago.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Window end (ISO 8601, exclusive). Omit for no upper bound.

get.description: Returns the Historian's hierarchical tag grouping (data sources) — useful for discovering what equipment exists.
Every tag property name defined on this Historian install.
Historian system configuration parameters. On-premises installs only — cloud Historian does not expose this entity.

Time-in-state breakdown (runtime / cip / idle / unknown) plus set run speed for one filler over a time window, derived from the machine's historian state tags. Backs the Portal's Machine Efficiency report via SunApps_Gateway. `until` is clamped to now.

Caveat: only Filler 1 currently has live machine-level historian tags. Fillers 2-6 return an all-unknown breakdown until their tags are historized.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Window end (ISO 8601). Must be after `since`; clamped to now.

schema.description: Hours per state (runtime / cip / idle / unknown) plus the set run speed.

get.summary: Filler 1 inlet flow volumes and trend for a window
get.description:
Windowed analytics for the Filler 1 inlet flow meter (TR11_FT1140 on the ThermaRoute leg from surge tanks ST81/82): totalizer first/last/delta with reset detection, total volume (odometer delta, falling back to integrated flow across a reset), volume split by machine state (runtime/cip/idle/unknown — the meter also counts flush/CIP water, so use `volume.byState.runtime` or `runs[]` for production volume, never the raw totalizer delta), per-run volumes, and trend points at a caller-chosen bucket resolution with explicit measured:false gaps. `until` is clamped to now.

Windows are caller-defined (ISO 8601, UTC, max 35 days) — the API deliberately has no shift/day bucketing or plant-timezone logic; anchor `since` to a shift boundary to get shift-aligned trend buckets. Historization of these tags began 2026-08-18T20:40Z; earlier windows return nulls, not errors. Requires the live AVEVA historian (returns 501 under the mock provider).

parameters.name: filler
parameters.description: Filler number. Only Filler 1 has an inlet flow meter.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Window end (ISO 8601). Must be after `since`; clamped to now.

parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: Trend bucket size in milliseconds (min 60000 = 1 minute; storage is minute-dense).

200.description: Flow volumes, runs, and trend for the window.

schema.description: totalizer {first,last,deltaGal,resetDetected}, volume {totalGal, method, integratedGal, byState}, runs[], trend[] (one point per expected bucket), coverage {bucketsExpected, bucketsMeasured, ...}.

501.description: The active historian provider (mock) cannot serve AnalogSummary queries.

get.description: Finished-good ⇐ raw-input pairings — the learned map of which raw input legitimately feeds which FG on a surge tank. A newly-observed combination lands here as `pending`; until it is approved, surge batches using it are held rather than posted to NetSuite.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by decision status. Omit for all.

post.description: Marks the FG ⇐ raw-input combination valid, so future surge batches using it post to NetSuite without being held.
Marks the FG ⇐ raw-input combination bad. Future surge batches using it are held for review instead of posting.
Rejects the wrong FG ⇐ raw-input combination and approves the corrected one in a single step — for when the observed raw input was mis-identified rather than simply invalid.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Pairing id of the incorrect combination.

rawInputItemId.description: NetSuite item id of the correct raw input.

rawInputName.description: Display name for the corrected raw input.

200.description: Pairing corrected — the bad combo is rejected and the correct one approved.

400.description: Invalid pairing id or missing correction details.

get.description: Full replay configuration plus live sim-clock state — what the UI banner reads to show whether the service is running against the real historian or replaying history.

replayMode.description: True when replaying historical data through the sim clock.

speedup.description: Sim clock multiplier — 60 means one simulated hour per real minute.

replayCrons.description: Cron expressions used while replay is on.

clock.description: Live sim clock state (current sim time

post.description:
Switches the service to the historical provider and starts the sim clock, so the cron jobs replay past plant activity instead of polling live. All in-memory job state is reset on the switch; DB rows are left alone. The body may update simStart / speedup / replayCrons at the same time.

Note this only changes where data is READ from — jobs still post to whatever NetSuite account is configured, so replaying against a production account will create real transactions.

simStart.description: Point in history to start replaying from.

replayCrons.description: Cron expressions to use while replaying.

200.description: Replay enabled — returns the new status.

post.description: Returns the service to its base provider (the `HISTORIAN_PROVIDER` env value, or `mock` when unset), restores the env cron schedule, and stops the sim clock. In-memory job state is reset on the switch; DB rows are left alone.

200.description: Replay disabled — returns the new status.

post.description: Updates simStart / speedup / replayCrons without toggling replay mode. Changes apply live if replay is currently on. At least one setting must be supplied.

200.description: Settings updated — returns the new status.

post.description: Freezes simulated time. Cron jobs keep firing but see a stationary clock, so replay stops advancing.

200.description: Clock paused — returns the current status.

post.description: Unfreezes simulated time after a pause.

200.description: Clock resumed — returns the current status.

post.description:
Wipes the service back to a clean slate for a fresh replay run. In order it rolls the sim clock back to `simStart`, clears every job's in-memory state and the status and poll stores, DELETES ALL ROWS from the MES batch tables (blend tank batches and inflows, pipe and surge issue states, surge tank batches, separation batches, bulk milk runs, inventory adjustments, the processing log, and FG input pairings), re-seeds the canonical FG input pairings, and then pm2-restarts the process so all state rehydrates from the emptied tables.

The response is sent BEFORE the restart, so a 200 means the truncation succeeded and the restart was scheduled — not that the service is back up. The restart is best-effort: outside pm2 it just logs a failure.

This deletes production MES history if pointed at a production database. There is no confirmation parameter and no authentication in front of it.

200.description: Tables cleared and a pm2 restart scheduled.

500.description: Reset failed before the response was sent.

get.description:
Returns the current cost constants used to price waste/shrink. An unseeded environment returns 200 with explicit nulls (consumers hide their $ figures) — never a 404. Pass `history=N` to also receive the most recent N price rows (max 100), newest first.
Also returns `families` — the current per-family raw milk prices (organic / conventional / a2 / cream_organic / cream_conventional), each `{ pricePerLb, source, basis, effectiveFrom }` where source is 'ns' (derived daily from NetSuite purchase transactions) or 'manual' (POST /raw-milk). Families with no price row yet are omitted. `history=N` additionally returns `familyHistory` (flat, newest first). The flat milkCostPerLb remains the fallback for batches no family classifies.

parameters.name: history
parameters.description: Also return the most recent N price rows.

schema.description: milkCostPerLb ($/lb), fgCasePrice ($/case, nullable), effectiveFrom, note; history[] when requested.

post.summary: Append a new cost row (becomes the current price)
post.description: Appends a price row — rows are never updated or deleted, so every change is audited. Also the post-deploy seed mechanism (see DEPLOY_CHECKLIST).

201.description: Row created; body is the new current constants.

post.summary: Append a manual per-family raw milk price row
post.description: Manual override / seed for one raw milk family — the only pricing path for families NetSuite can't derive (A2 has no priced purchase transactions). Append-only, like the flat costs. NOTE — for families the daily NS sync CAN derive, a manual row stands only until the next sync finds a differing NS price and re-asserts it.

201.description: Row created; body is the new current row for that family.

get.description: The item groups the BOM admin UI offers as starting points — surge finished goods, batch goods, and raw items — plus the surge-FG → batch-twin map that pairs each finished good with the batch item representing the same product mid-process.
Free-text search over NetSuite assembly items — the fallback when the item isn't in one of the predefined groups.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search text matched against item name / id.

get.description: Components of the item's current (default) BOM revision.

post.description: Validates a proposed component list against the item's current BOM revision and returns the diff — including circular-reference checks — without writing anything to NetSuite. Run this before `/commit`.

400.description: Missing itemId or the proposed BOM is invalid.

post.description: OVERWRITES the components of the item's current BOM revision in live NetSuite. Destructive and not versioned by this service — preview first.

components.description: Component lines that will replace the revision's current lines.

400.description: Missing itemId or the commit was rejected.

post.summary: Bulk-set surge FG BOMs to their batch twin
post.description: Sets every surge finished good's BOM to a single line — 1 lb of its batch twin. Dry-run by default; pass `commit: true` to actually write to live NetSuite across every surge FG at once.

commit.description: false (default) previews the changes; true writes them to NetSuite.

get.description: Paged, filterable, sortable list of blend tank batches for the analytics table.
Blend tank output bucketed over time for the trend chart.
Paged, filterable, sortable list of surge tank batches.
Surge tank output bucketed over time for the trend chart.
Paged, filterable, sortable list of separator batches.

parameters.name: sourceSilo
parameters.description: Restrict to batches drawn from one raw milk silo.

get.description: Separator throughput bucketed over time for the trend chart.
Inventory adjustments this service generated from historian tank-level movements — the shrink/gain postings that reconcile NetSuite inventory to what the plant floor actually measured.

parameters.name: excludePositiveSilo
parameters.description: Drop positive silo adjustments, which are usually refills rather than true gains.

get.description: Same rows and filters as `/inventory-adjustments`, but each row carries a `correlation` block tracing the adjustment back to the work order, assembly unbuild, or batch that caused it — plus a `correlationStats` summary of how confidently the matches were made.

200.description: Adjustments with per-row correlation and a correlationStats summary.

get.description: The batch-centric inverse of the correlations view — each batch in the window with the inventory adjustments attributed to it and per-batch rollups. Drives the Batch Adjustments page.

parameters.name: onlyWithAdjustments
parameters.description: Drop batches that have no correlated adjustments.

get.description: Pulls the batch's real transactions (issues, completions, unbuilds, adjustments) live from NetSuite by the internal ids this service recorded — source-of-truth reconciliation for when the local record and NetSuite are suspected to disagree.

Everything about a single batch for the batch-detail page — the full record, correlated inventory adjustments and their rollup, transaction counts and the processing log, bins, lots, ingredient inflows, and separation destinations. A local read; use the `/netsuite` variant to reconcile against NetSuite itself.
Adjustment quantities bucketed over time for the trend chart.

post.description: Re-posts an errored or skipped adjustment to NetSuite, optionally with operator corrections to the bin, item, quantity or lot. Backs the Retry button on the Inventory Adjustment Review screen. Writes to live NetSuite.
Dismisses an adjustment that should not post (status becomes `rejected`). Nothing is written to NetSuite.

400.description: Adjustment not found or reject failed.

get.description: Reports uptime, which historian provider is currently active (`RestProvider`, `MockProvider`, or `HistoricalProvider` while replay mode is on), and the last poll timestamp for the separation, bulk milk and blend tank jobs. Used by the deploy workflow's smoke check.

historianProvider.description: Class name of the active provider.
